written.text: Write a precis of the following passage in about one third of the original length and suggest a suitable title.(10) Skill-based training today is no longer what it used to be. With rapid technological progress and changing industry requirements, older methods of teaching—mainly based on memorization and repetition—have become insufficient. Workers in modern industries are expected not only to possess technical knowledge but also to demonstrate adaptability, problem-solving ability, and readiness to work with new technologies. At this point, the role of instructors in Industrial Training Institutes becomes especially important. Their responsibility goes beyond delivering lessons; they are expected to connect theoretical learning with practical application. By guiding trainees to think independently and solve real-life problems, instructors help them become more confident and capable. This also means that instructors themselves must regularly upgrade their skills and remain aware of current industrial practices. The introduction of digital tools and simulation methods has improved the training process. Yet, these tools alone cannot guarantee effective learning. If not guided properly, trainees may perform tasks without understanding the basic concepts behind them. Therefore, it is necessary to maintain a balance between hands-on practice and conceptual clarity. In the end, the goal of industrial training is to develop workers who are skilled, confident, and adaptable. This goal can be achieved only when instructors take on the role of mentors who encourage continuous learning.

Many students avoid vocational training and choose general academic courses without a proper career plan. Write a letter to the Editor of the daily newspaper Zawlkhawpui discussing this issue and suggesting ways to increase awareness of skilled jobs.Address yourself as XXX.(10)

Read the following passage carefully and answer the following questions: Industrial training plays an important role in preparing young people for employment. It focuses on developing practical skills that are directly useful in the workplace. However, many trainees do not fully benefit from such training because they lack seriousness and discipline. Some attend classes irregularly, while others do not pay attention during practical sessions. Instructors try to guide trainees by demonstrating correct methods and encouraging them to practice regularly. Still, without interest and effort from the trainees, learning remains incomplete. In addition, the proper use of tools and safety measures is often ignored, which can lead to accidents. To make training effective, both instructors and trainees must work together. Trainees should take responsibility for their learning, while instructors should create an engaging and supportive environment. Only then can industrial training achieve its goal of producing skilled and confident workers. (i)What is the main purpose of industrial training?(2) (ii)Why do some trainees fail to benefit fully from training?(2) (iii)What role do instructors play in the training process?(2) (iv)How can industrial training be made more effective?(2) (v)Find a word from the passage similar in meaning to “self-control.”(1) (vi)Find a word from the passage opposite in meaning to “comprehensive.”(1)
